question.problem:
Find, to three decimal places, the interquartile range of the random variable $X$ if the cumulative distribution function of $X$ is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1, \\ 1-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find the interquartile range, we first need to find the lower quartile and the upper quartile.

The lower quartile of a random variable $X$ is the number ${q}_{1}$ such that

$$
P(X\le {q}_{1})=\frac{1}{4},
$$

and the upper quartile is the number ${q}_{3}$ such that

$$
P(X\le {q}_{3})=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

First, we find the lower quartile:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le {q}_{1}) & =\frac{1}{4} \\ F({q}_{1}) & =\frac{1}{4} \\ 1-\frac{1}{{{q}_{1}}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{1}{{{q}_{1}}^{2}} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ {q}_{1} & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the upper quartile:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le {q}_{3}) & =\frac{3}{4} \\ F({q}_{3}) & =\frac{3}{4} \\ 1-\frac{1}{{{q}_{3}}^{2}} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ \frac{1}{{{q}_{3}}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ {q}_{3} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the interquartile range is

$$
IQR={q}_{3}-{q}_{1}=2-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}≈0.845
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
